service.name: Wedding and corporate event DJ
service.serviceType: Open-format DJ for weddings, corporate events, late-night receptions and private parties
service.description: Open-format DJ for wedding receptions, corporate events and private parties across Denver and the Colorado mountain corridor, on its own or carrying the late night after a band through the same sound system on one contract.

faqs.q: Can the DJ follow the band on the same contract?
faqs.a: Yes. Once we are in the building the evening is already committed, so adding the DJ to a band booking costs far less than hiring one separately would, through the same sound system and on the same invoice. The handoff is planned against your run of show.

faqs.q: Do you DJ weddings as well as corporate events?
faqs.a: Yes. The wedding booking usually starts at the end of dinner, with live players in front of it for the ceremony and the cocktail hour, and the DJ carrying the floor from the first dance to the last song. It is the same open-format set, the same sound system and the same contract as the corporate night, and the ceremony and cocktail hour pages cover the hours before it.

faqs.q: What does the DJ booking include?
faqs.a: Decks, booth and a PA sized to the venue, a dedicated announcement microphone on its own channel, load-in and strike, a certificate of insurance naming your venue, a W-9 and one itemised invoice. Sound is inside the published figure at every size, this one included.

faqs.q: How late can the DJ play?
faqs.a: As late as the venue allows. Added time bills at the same hourly rate in 30-minute increments, agreed on the night with whoever holds the budget, and there is no overtime rate. Venue curfews and decibel caps are honoured as written and built into the plan at contract.

faqs.q: What is the DJ plus live instrument option?
faqs.a: A live bass or saxophone played on the floor over the set. It reads as a crowd watching something happen rather than a playlist, and it holds a dance floor late. It is a named option, quoted as its own line when you ask for it.

faqs.q: Do you take requests on the night?
faqs.a: From you, always, and from guests where they fit. A do-not-play list is the part worth spending time on before the event. A request that would empty the floor gets a straight answer and an alternative.
